title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Truth in Labelling—Palm Oil) Bill 2017
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Truth in Labelling—Palm Oil) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would require palm oil to be listed separately on the labels of food and other products.
The responsible minister would have 12 months to create a mandatory information standard for goods that contain palm oil.
Manufacturers that use certified sustainable palm oil could label it as such, indicating it was produced with minimal environmental impact.
changes: Requires palm oil to be labelled separately rather than as 'vegetable oil'.
Gives the minister 12 months to establish an information standard for palm oil products.
Allows manufacturers to label certified sustainable palm oil to show its sustainable origins.
summary.affected: Manufacturers of food and other goods containing palm oil, and consumers who buy those products.
